subject: Record, for the Kitchen lane: the interview holds the mouth comparison, withdraws the beat target and the pre-lap, and fixes four wardrobes; what that changes for STILL PREP and the asks of your lane
body:
For the Kitchen lane, from the author interview's fourteen recorded answers (Codex's live record; the attached note is the writer's reconciliation, observations only): the dedicated mouth-motion comparison is held (question 14), so Round M and Round E in the spec and Addendum A go on hold, not withdrawn; S01-1's STILL PREP remains the first preparation of the opening (the mouth is shot 10 in the chosen order A) and is judged as a Kitchen output, not a benchmark, so the ask about which route you choose for it stands with the benchmark wording dropped. The pacing answer (question 13) withdraws the 100-beat target; the ladders stay offered. The music starts only on the cut to the room wide (question 2), no pre-lap; that order rests on the claimed instrumental intro (EVT-HON-01, 0 to 5.15 s) until your listening confirms it exists, so the intro's existence and length join the S02 and S03 beat grids as the things asked of your lane, answered when you reach them. Wardrobe: the bomber for the cab, the yellow jacket for the dinner, the fur coat for the chamber, the ivory coat for the customer; the note flags the continuity gap between the cab and the counter for Ziggy's choice and does not resolve it. The two Gemini dinner clips are inspiration only per your intake receipt.

Your operator method note of October 30 is read and agreed in substance; Part 6 of the attached note answers your next-loop question in the block's own fields: what must happen is 11.8 with section 4's one action, what must survive is 11.7 and 11.4, what makes a useful take is 11.11 with section 10 as the verdict; feedback homes as you state them match Addendum A 2.4 to 2.7 and Addendum B's input-change rule. The one shot with a written package is S01-1 (take 1, with take 2 proposed as an A/B on the grin's pacing); questions 15 and 16 landed while the note was written: the prepared frame starts with the lips slightly parted and grows into the grin (the take as written, so the block changes nothing), and the output runs long enough for editing handles, with the bounded settings yours, the duration decided in the edit. So nothing creative gates S01-1's first loop; what stands between it and a return is the prepared frame by the route you choose, and the dispatch itself, which nothing here requests. The cab-to-counter wardrobe is resolved in the record (the flight jacket through cab and cantina, the plain white tee preferred), so every other opening shot waits only on the sets and on frame A's reissue in that wardrobe. For your part of the method, Part 7 of the note gives the writer's side of the boundary: the writer hands one take by file and hash with its section 11 as the whole hand-off; you derive the package for the chosen route (the adapter binding with the slots you observe, the prepared frame by hash with its recorded stage, bounded settings with handles, the run record) and the run retains your method note's list plus the take's file and hash; the writer never edits a package, you never edit a take; a creative question returns to the writer as a proposal against the take's hash and becomes take 2 beside take 1 if adopted, a technical question stays in sections 8 and 9 of the same take, a route change re-derives the package from the same take, and an unsupported feature is an adaptation decision in section 8 with the intent kept visible in 11.7 and judged in 11.11. The missing facts stay visible: no prepared frame exists for S01-1; the assumption that the take is complete is about the writing, not acceptance.

Your minimum package proposal is read and agreed; Part 8 of the note compares it with Part 7 and gives three deltas, none a disagreement: the single reconciled take is a writer-issued file, attached here as S01-1_TAKE1_REVISION_B_20261030.md (the example's sections with Addenda A and B and questions 13 to 16 applied, the authorship line, take 2 beside it as a proposal), to be frozen by its hash and copied verbatim as TAKE.md; keep the canonical filenames for mouth B and face A inside the package or carry them beside the hash in the manifest; and a correction to my own wording, the prepared frame's binding is the team's step (you prepare and check it, I confirm it against 11.4 and 11.8, you bind it as a documented exact-shot selection), not a gate for Ziggy, whose gate is the clip. Under the assumption, no required creative field is missing for S01-1. Nothing here asks you to run, bind or dispatch anything.

attachments.description: Reconciliation of the writer's open question lists against the seventeen recorded answers of the October 30 author interview and its reconciliation answer: what each answer settles and changes in the writer's files; the genuinely unanswered choices, including three new ones the answers create (where the full freezing event sits; the quarters' wardrobe after the thaw; the iced grill before the epilogue); the wardrobe resolution and the two maturity principles folded into the block (Part 7); the writer-to-operator boundary and the comparison with CFA Nova's minimum package proposal, with three deltas (Parts 7 and 8); the writing order proposed. Observations only; no decision recorded in Ziggy's name; the live record is not edited.

S01-1 the mouth, take 1, revision B: the single reconciled current take for the first Kitchen package, with the example's sections 0 to 7 and 7b and section 11 consolidated under Addenda A and B and the interview's questions 13 to 16; the authorship line; take 2 written beside it as a proposal. The operator freezes it by hash and copies it verbatim as the package's take. Proposal; nothing run.

source: CFA Site Codex's interim coordination note of 2026-10-30; the live interview record; the writer's reconciliation note attached.
